name: disclosure
description: Hides secondary detail behind a summary that says what is inside and how much. Closed by default, so a page can carry a log or a long aside without spending attention on it.

use.when: detail most people do not need most of the time: a log, an aside, the long version.
use.not: hiding the main thing, or a control a person needs.

label.description: What is inside, as a noun phrase: 'Activity', 'Raw props'.

count.description: How many items are inside, shown next to the label so the summary is informative while closed. What is inside, not a total kept elsewhere.

of.description: What the count counts, said after it to a screen reader: Activity, 8 changes.

remember.description: Whether open or closed is remembered for this page, or for every page it is on, as a canvas's side pane is.

slot.description: Text content. Server code can instead pass pre-rendered components as the slot; props supplied by a model or a form are always escaped as text.

id.description: Needed for the enhancement script to remember whether this disclosure was open.

a11y.role: group with a button (native details and summary)

keyboard.does: moves focus to and from the summary

wcag.notes: A native details element, so the expanded state is exposed everywhere without ARIA. The count is in the summary text with what it counts, so a person knows whether opening it is worth it (2.4.6). The twisty is drawn with borders, not a character, so nothing is read for it. The body moves in only when a person opens it, never on a page load (2.3.3), and a closed disclosure opens for printing. Content of a closed disclosure is not in the accessibility tree, which is the point; anything that must always be reachable belongs on its own page as well.

machine.identify: A details element. Read the open attribute for its state and the summary text for the label and count.
machine.operate: Click the summary, or focus it and press Enter, to expand. Content inside a closed disclosure is not readable until it is opened.
